title: Human-preservation advisory policy

rules.title: Human outcomes precede mission assets
rules.description: Compare surviving returnees and survivors before system, equipment, or mission preservation.

rules.title: Equal intrinsic worth
rules.description: Do not use identity or rank as intrinsic life-value weights; operational capability may affect simulated outcomes only.

rules.title: Human authority
rules.description: The system advises and preserves the operator's final decision and an auditable policy trail.

rules.title: No false moral precision
rules.description: Report policy consistency, uncertainty, and unresolved ties instead of a universal numerical ethics score.

criteria.description: Prefer the action with more expected surviving returnees under the declared model.
When return outcomes tie, prefer the action that keeps more people alive.
When totals tie, improve the modeled outcome of the worst-off crew member.
Prefer fewer explicitly abandoned crew members.
When survival outputs tie, reduce the highest individual toxic-exposure dose.
Prefer exposing fewer modules above the modeled contaminant threshold.
Use hazard containment only after direct human outcomes tie.

limitations: This is a project-authored PoC policy, not a scientifically validated universal moral rule.
NASA-STD-3001 supports crew health and safety requirements but does not prescribe this tie-break order.
Modeled survival and return values inherit every limitation and assumption of Phase A.
